newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber market ends down on liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber market ends down on liquidation.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market posted slight losses at the close on Tuesday due to modest liquidation in the market, dealers said.
"Some people were liquidating their positions in the market. The level of activity was not really that heavy," a dealer said, adding easier prices in Japan kept sentiment in the market bearish.

Another dealer said there was also a "bit of covering by manufacturers who were trying to get material for their monthly needs. Most of the deals were for nearby months, but it was just mostly routine business."
Traders said the bulk of covering was seen in deals for prompt shipment of RSS3 grade rubber. There was a large deal done for a forward shipment of RSS1 rubber.
The market was subdued because several industry officials were also at meetings of the International Rubber Study Group and the annual rubber trade forum in Liverpool, England.

At 0945 GMT, July RSS3 was seen at 114.50 U.S. cents a kg from 115.25 cents. July RSS1 was seen at 162.00 Singapore cents (US$1.13) a kg from 163.00 cents. July TSR20 was seen at 148.50 Singapore cents (US$1.03) a kg from 149.25 cents.
